steps.user_message: Can you help me finalize the catering for the team lunch with our new client, Ms. Samantha Lee, on Thursday, September 9th at 12:00 PM in the conference room?
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should acknowledge and remember: Can you help me finalize the catering for the team lunch with our new client, Ms. Samantha Lee, on Thursday, September 9th at 12:00 PM in the conference room?
steps.agent_response:
Absolutely — I can help. I can draft/send messages to the caterer, to Ms. Samantha Lee (the client), and/or to the internal team so everything’s confirmed. Before I act, a few quick questions and options so I get it right:

Questions I need answered
1. Which year should I use for Sep 9? (And your time zone, if that matters for timing.)  
2. Who should I contact to place the order? (Caterer name/email or your office manager’s email — or should I search your inbox for previous caterer contacts?)  
3. Final headcount (approx.) and any known dietary restrictions (vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free/halal/kosher/allergies)?  
4. Budget or menu preferences (boxed lunches, buffet, plated, cuisine types, allergies-safe choices)?  
5. Delivery/setup time (do you want catering delivered at 11:30 AM to allow setup, or another time?) and any special requests (plates/utensils/napkins/tablecloths, labeled meals, signs)?  
6. Billing details: charge to company card, expense report, or pay on invoice? Who is the billing contact?  
7. Do you want Ms. Samantha Lee included in menu decisions or just informed/confirmed? If you’d like me to email her, I’ll need her email address.

Suggested messages (I can send or save as drafts)
- To caterer (example subject/body)
  Subject: Catering request — Team lunch with client Thu, Sep 9 at 12:00 PM (Conference room)
  Body: Hello [Caterer Name],  
  We need catering for a team lunch with a client on Thursday, September 9 at 12:00 PM in our conference room. Details:  
  - Headcount: [XX]  
  - Delivery/setup: [e.g., 11:30 AM to conference room]  
  - Menu preferences: [e.g., boxed lunches with one vegetarian and one gluten-free option; or buffet with salad, two mains, two sides, desserts]  
  - Dietary restrictions/allergies: [list]  
  - Supplies needed: plates, utensils, napkins (please confirm)  
  - Billing: [company card / invoice to Billing Dept — provide billing contact if needed]  
  Please send menu options and pricing by [deadline, e.g., 3 business days before] and confirm availability. Thank you — [Your Name, Phone]

- To Ms. Samantha Lee (client) — optional
  Subject: Team lunch on Thu, Sep 9 at 12:00 PM — quick confirmation
  Body: Hi Ms. Lee,  
  Looking forward to meeting you for lunch on Thursday, September 9 at 12:00 PM in our conference room. Is that time still good for you? Also, do you have any dietary restrictions or preferences we should accommodate?  
  Best, [Your Name]

- To internal team / organizer
  Subject: Catering for client lunch — Thu Sep 9, 12:00 PM — please RSVP
  Body: Quick note: We’re arranging catering for the team lunch with Ms. Samantha Lee on Thu, Sep 9 at 12:00 PM in the conference room. Planned headcount: [XX]. Please reply with attendance and any dietary restrictions by [deadline]. I’ll confirm the order afterward.

- Draft one or more of the emails above and save to Drafts for your review.  
- Send any of the above immediately (I’ll need the recipient email addresses and any placeholders filled).  
- Search your inbox for previous caterer contacts or past orders to reuse.  
- Create a short menu/options email to the caterer asking for a few preset packages if you’d like.

Tell me which action to take and provide the missing details (year, headcount, dietary needs, caterer or recipient emails, and whether to notify Ms. Lee). I’ll draft or send the emails accordingly.
